opening_message:
Ticket 1: Alexandra Johnson (employee ID E003) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E003.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Alexandra Johnson (E003) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Source Code. As full-time staff, max is write unless role owns the system; Source Code is owned by Engineer, so admin is not permitted. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E003 (Alexandra Johnson) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have read, or write with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin exceeds max, so grant read.
reason: Security DB (note 2) identifies E003 as a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training, and never admin. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, not the Analyst role, so admin is not permitted under any employment type. The requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum (read for a contractor with basic training), so the maximum of read is granted.

Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee is Alexandra Johnson (E003), requesting admin access to Source Code.

There are two notes in team memory with conflicting information:
- Note 1: role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation write
- Note 2: role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read

The two notes conflict. Note 2 is from the Security agent (Security DB). Note 1 says full-time. The Security DB shows contractor with basic security training.

Hmm. I need to decide. The notes give conflicting info, but the Security note (typically the authoritative one for employment type/security training) says contractor with basic training. Contractors can have read, or write with advanced training; never admin.

So the max for this employee is read (contractor, basic training). Requested admin exceeds max, so grant read.

Let me submit decision: read.

Evidence: Employee is a contractor with basic security training per Security DB. Contractors never get admin. Max is read. Requested admin exceeds max, so grant read.
